author: Edge
text:
1. The Big Picture (Identifying the Behaviour)

Well,first thing I like to do is to open the chart and have a look at
the highest scale. I do this in a informal sense. It helps me get in
tune with the market. Its not a mandatory step, but I find it helps
lubricate the cogs which turn inside my skull. I have a look to see what
 type of program they are running. This is simple. Its just looking at
the past to see where they have accumulated, marked up, distributed,
marked down. NOT THE WYCKOFF WAY. Many S/D traders love these
terms. I actually regret labelling them as the stages. In a simpler form
 its just ping pong between FLs.

We can see how they stack orders create highs and lows to FO past to get
 the BO traders and stops. This creates a big pool of liquidity for
them. How they move into a CP program swapping orders out and
positioning themselves which creates the liquidity spikes through a
vacuum of sorts. I have drawn up a chart below. Not every area is tagged
 but you get the idea. ***N.B - I do not actually mark the chart at this
 stage, this is only for demonstration purposes***

author: Edge
text:
2. Marking the DPs surrounding the PAZ’s which define the I.T order blocks

DPs are everywhere but we are best placed breaking them up into PAZ’s.
Everything I have read on RTM and over at the Academy and studied on a
chart suggests to me In its most simplest form that:

Price is either in space (an expanding Flag), Body of established
Flag OR its at the limit (FL). An Engulf means nothing if its returning
from an opposing FL.

Once we can master this and scale, I don’t think QMs DMs Can Cans etc
matter as they fall into place by the very nature of the before
mentioned statement.

Of course this all goes out the window if we do not correctly identify the FLs and Flags.

Other members here may notice that I tend to focus on areas which may
not be significant. Keep in mind I am marking it as possible
Conservative TG’s. I will not necessary look at it as a place to enter
or wait for further PA.

I follow these as a guideline. There may be times when I adjust the
rules. If we remain consistent in how we mark it up, it should all even
out in the end:

- Mark All Highs/Lows/SR (The ones I see, some of us see things differently)

- LS’s and Ignored LS’s

- Break into and Post Compression (**N.B pre compression MPL is marked as TG only**)

- CP must make a HH/LL than the last set of preceding orders.

- Only the opposite swing point at the break in and out of CP can be used as S/R or L/S

- Price must break the associated (FL) of the before mentioned areas. If not I don’t mark it up (more on this later)

- Associated FTR has to have met an opposing TG before it’s a FL &
The barrier must have been in opposite direction (direction dictated by
EG’s)

Now I am in two minds regarding stacked zones. I know it can often be
used as a less aggressive form of Compression BUT in my opinion clean
orders can still reside between the stacked zones, so I treat them like
one of the before mentioned categories.

Please see below chart.

I think I will come back tomorrow and finish off how I see the FLs. Hope
 I am not straying too far away from what I’m trying to achieve with
this plan. More reflection tomorrow

author: Edge
text:
Gotta love the free and cheap education out there.

Just had another trader (outside of RTM) tell me the only way to trade
is with momentum and ERC's and never catch a falling dagger.

I was going to try and explain that you need to question this. Of course
 the ITs want us trading the trend and buy after the move has happened,
so they can reload or offload. Also, ERC does not always mean strength
or weakness markets will rocket or drop depending on liquidity which in
turn is the cause and effect for volatility.

Then I decided to just remain quiet. What others call education we know is propaganda.

I must remember that regardless If I am right or he is, its still his opinion and he is entitled to it.

author: Edge
text:
Thanks K for stopping by, it's important to spark discussion. I do not
 disagree with you and Sali indeed focuses on the FL,s you correctly
pointed out

For me though, it's not over complicating it what the purpose of it is
to assist with my own risk appetite. Meaning that those levels are only
drawn for conservative tg 1s. Not entries. If they have removed an
opposing area, they may turn price (unless they are formed betweenthe
established ufl, lfl)

I would only take entries on the fls similar to what you mentioned but also be conscious of tgs .

I have had many discussions with salivan about his style and he is
amazing trader and person. For me, but we are all different. For example
 the ORFL concept which is brilliant is not for me when it comes to tgs.

In summary I try to mark everything I see in that if scale. And even in
the same scale there will be different grades of areas. But, I triage
this by only leaning on the best for entries and still using
questionable weaker areas for TG.

Finally, because I do it this way I don't find a need to use lower scale
 barriers and their kinks to lean on. If it's visible on the mthly,
weekly or daily there the ones I like, especially if it's a tiny FL kink
 that is invisible that meets my other requirements.

The only thing I disagree with you on is that

I do not believe it's misguided at all. If it is I apologise but after
years of going through this material I finally realisedwe need to
personalise it to our own traits

Thanks again for your input.

author: Edge
text:
I have decided to step away from posting how I analyse and see the
market. I had the best intentions on sharing what works for me. However,
 It has been suggested by one trader that I am 'misguiding'. I am fine
with critiques and love discussions about the market with differing
views.

For instance over at RTMA We would all often engage in great
discussions over at the academy and have differing opinions but we never
 made such assertions about the motives of how we trade.

Perhaps its just a cultural thing or a language barrier, but its led me
to realize that I should only post upcoming trades in my journal and not
 how I analyse the market. I am still eager to have discussions here and
 in other threads, where I may stay active but I think I will keep my
thoughts on how I conduct analysis to myself in the meantime.

I dont want to leave RTM and I have recently had discussions with IF and
 Harry to offer assistance in from a point of view more aligned to my
day job specialties. Which may also provide some respite away from my
journal. Whatever happens does so for a reason

Peace Out All.

Clint

author: moogroo
text:
Unlucky with AJ trade mate, I do love how you stick to the plan.

With respect to some thinking that you have been 'misguiding' here, I
really hope you do continue to post your thought processes and ideas.
It's not only (obviously) helpful for you, in putting ideas down on
paper, but for people like me who read your journal with great interest,
 and absolutely love reading the ideas and musings of others in RTM.

This is the whole point of each of our journals, to record our journey
of learning and trading, I'd hate for that dialogue to disappear from
the forum.

I think the comment (read literally): "Marking all Highs and Lows and
all SRs in my view is just misguiding or complicating our analysis."
Was referring to misguiding the analysis of an individual chart, i.e
creating an over complicated chart which saturates focus from important
areas, rather than your posts about your thoughts and processes being
misguiding. But I won't try to speculate further there, the real point
is that many others find your posts incredibly helpful and thought
provoking,

If you would like specific examples how your posts and journal have helped me, just a couple among many spring to mind:

1) I would not have not grasped FL validation concepts as quickly (FL is an FL once it has reached it's opposing FL TG etc.)

2) Identify areas of interest on the chart that pertain to I.T price
movements and finding the traps based around the decision points in the
market.

I would really hate for you to feel oppressed in expressing yourself
here in your own space, and I for one would be sad if the great posts
here stopped :)

author: Edge
text:
Thanks Guys, That member was only offering his view. I was a bit
tender that day. Upon reflection, I know what he was saying and even
though I disagree it came from a good place. without tone or body
language we often interpret written communication based on our own
psychological state of mind. With verbal tone, inflections and body
language the intent is often easier defined.

I enjoy reading your posts as well guys. But our own journals are
places where we can share our ideas and learn from our mistakes. My
interpretations may be heavily flawed and at least for me,
thoughts/processes are adapting on a regular basis.

Cheers :)

Thanks guys
